content:
mike: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal to add a tiny Contract Adapter service between api-gateway and runtime to canonicalize request shapes + provide backward compatibility for legacy clients.

sara: TL;DR: small shim that normalizes inputs, handles versioned fields, and centralizes a few messy rules we have spread across 3 services. keeps runtime simple. :+1:

jordan: can you sketch failure modes? curious about perf and added latency for hotpath.

mike: perf is main concern. goal: keep adapter off hot GPU path for steady-state by making it stateless and autoscaling on small CPU instances. expected median added p95 ~ 8-12ms on warm paths.

nate: do we plan to run this in front of Dedicated pools too? latency budget tighter there.

mike: yes but with config flags per deployment. for Dedicated we will allow bypass (runtime-side tenant pinning) once tenants migrate. adapter will carry a header x-contract-version so runtime can short-circuit.

sara: concrete responsibilities:
- canonicalize chat/message shapes (role/name/content → unified 'utterance')
- normalize tool-call/func schema to single field set
- dedupe repeated prompt prefixes (cheap prefix-trim cache)
- emit normalized telemetry tags for quality regression linking

jordan: sounds good. where's ownership? infra or eng-runtime?

mike: propose eng-runtime owns the adapter code, eng-infra owns deployment/scale config. reduces cross-team touches for logic changes.

sara: rollout plan suggestion:
1) land adapter behind a feature flag in frontend gateway (no traffic)
2) enable for small % of internal/testing tenants, compare telemetry
3) enable for low-traffic external tenants; run dual-write telemetry (pre/post canonicalized)
4) iterate rules -> remove dup logic from downstream services
5) toggle bypass for Dedicated when tenant ready

nate: what about contracts for evals/QA? we need a way to pin an adapter rule-set to an eval run.

mike: will add a rule-set-id header that eval harness can set; also keep rule-set manifest in S3 + rollout metadata.

jordan: need example config snippet for adapter rules so reviewers can vet.

sara: posting quick example: 
```json
{
  "rule_set_id": "v1.0.0",
  "normalize": {
    "chat": {"role_map": {"assistant": "system"}, "strip_empty_names": true},
    "tool_calls": {"allow_unknown_fn": false, "map_args": "flatten"}
  },
  "dedupe": {"prefix_seconds": 120},
  "emit_tags": ["adapter_v1","canonicalized"]
}
```

mike: perfect. perf experiment idea: run adapter in-line for 5% of traffic and also send the raw request to an async tracer to compute divergence but not double-process. keeps runtime load constant.

nate: sounds safe. what about error handling? adapter should never 5xx for client errors; must convert bad shapes -> 400 with helpful message. runtime-only failures should be triaged separately.

jordan: plus a fallback path: if adapter latency > 200ms or error-rate spike, gateway should bypass adapter and attach header x-adapter-bypassed=reason. auto-rollbacks for spikes.

sara: ops checklist for rollout:
- dashboard for adapter latency/error by tenant
- canary rule-set diff viewer (pre/post normalized sample)
- alarm on mismatch rate > 1% for critical tenants
- migration runbook to move downstream rule logic into adapter

mike: action items: 
- @jordan to draft lightweight adapter API + health contract (this week)
- @sara to assemble rule-set manifest and sample mappings (EOD Wednesday)
- @nate to sketch infra autoscaling + bypass feature flag options

alexa-bot: deploy-bot: created channel alert terraform PR #412 for adapter canary alarms (link: https://git.redwood/infra/pr/412)

jordan: I'll put a spike branch up tomorrow with a minimal adapter that just remaps chat shape and emits tags. want simple perf harness with 10k synthetic requests.

mike: cool. final note: keep adapter small and replaceable. long-term idea is to fold some of this into gateway if it proves ultra-low cost, but shipping stand-alone reduces blast radius.

sara: agreed. sounds like a plan. :rocket:

mike: thanks all — will track in the refactor epic and link the RFC follow-up.
